scenarios.title: Governments deploy opaque AI profiling to decide immigration and public benefit claims
scenarios.world: It is 2029. In several European and North American jurisdictions, border authorities and welfare agencies rely on proprietary automated platforms to summarize applicant interviews, assess asylum seeker ages, inspect mobile device archives, and score relationship authenticity. When applicants are flagged as high-risk or rejected, caseworkers rubber-stamp automated recommendations because caseload volumes prevent independent review. Government agencies invoke state secrecy exemptions to withhold training data and scoring logic from public courts and legal aid solicitors, leaving vulnerable individuals unable to challenge biased model outputs or opaque algorithmic classifications.
scenarios.premise: Government ministries increasingly integrate generative language models and automated scoring systems into border management, asylum claim processing, and identity screening. Because these tools are introduced under national security exemptions without public transparency or individual recourse, algorithmic errors and uncalibrated proxies harden into institutional barriers.
scenarios.how: Independent technical observatories monitor public-sector algorithmic procurement, measuring accuracy drift, proxy discrimination, and procedural opacity across deployed administrative systems. By providing open-source verification tooling, local-first data custody, and cryptographic audit receipts, decentralized networks equip legal clinics and individuals to challenge ungrounded administrative claims without surrendering private personal information to cloud databases.

outcomes.name: State agencies hide automated decision algorithms behind national security secrecy
outcomes.description: Bureaucracies expand automated risk profiling into routine public administration while shielding model logic and error rates from judicial discovery.
outcomes.example: An asylum applicant in London is denied protection after an automated summarization model misinterprets translated testimony, while immigration tribunals uphold the decision citing national security exemptions that block release of the model prompt and verification log.

outcomes.name: Civic cooperatives provide independent algorithmic audits and verification receipts
outcomes.description: Digital rights organizations, legal aid clinics, and community cooperatives deploy independent verification tooling and verifiable audit trails to challenge uncalibrated administrative scoring.
outcomes.example: A legal advocacy coalition uses cryptographic verification tooling to prove that an administrative agency's age-estimation model produces contradictory outputs across different seeds, forcing statutory disclosure and human procedural review.

outcomes.name: Public agencies replace automated scoring with even harsher administrative restrictions
outcomes.description: In response to judicial pushback against opaque automated profiling, political administrations impose rigid statutory quotas and across-the-board processing freezes that bypass algorithmic scrutiny entirely.
outcomes.example: Facing public lawsuits over algorithmic bias in asylum summarization, a border department cancels automated pilots and instead enforces arbitrary numerical caps on daily visa approvals, leaving applicants with fewer avenues for individual review.

scenarios.title: Personal AI agents negotiate privacy rules with websites instead of showing cookie popups
scenarios.world: It is 2029. Most people browse the web using compact, open models running directly inside their devices. Commercial websites no longer display intrusive cookie banners or dark-pattern consent notices; instead, their servers broadcast structured privacy contracts to visiting agents. A reader visiting an online news portal never sees a popup. Behind the scenes, their local personal assistant checks the site's data requests against a private, locally stored policy. Routine functional cookies for font caching and site styling are granted temporary, non-identifying tokens automatically, while a hidden request to link browsing habits to cross-site identity brokers is immediately rejected with a cryptographic refusal receipt. When an unfamiliar healthcare directory requests permission to save diagnostic search terms, the user's assistant pauses and prompts the user with a plain-language summary before releasing any facts.
scenarios.premise: Manipulative consent banners and cookie walls are failing as automated browser agents interact with web services on behalf of people. When websites shift to machine-readable consent protocols, user-owned edge agents can negotiate minimal ephemeral data exchanges locally while escalating risky tracking requests.
scenarios.how: The open collective provides browser-based personal twin software that executes directly on user hardware, validating machine-readable consent requests against explicit authority envelopes, generating structured audit logs, and keeping all personal evaluation local.

outcomes.name: Platforms deploy deceptive machine-to-machine consent negotiations
outcomes.description: Commercial tracking networks build automated consent endpoints that overwhelm user agents with complex legalistic micro-requests, tricking simple automated models into granting persistent telemetry scopes.
outcomes.example: A student using a generic browser agent visits an online textbook repository that silently requests background telemetry under a necessary performance label, which the agent routinely approves without notifying the student.

outcomes.name: Local guardian agents enforce verifiable minimal consent receipts
outcomes.description: Standardized, user-controlled local agents evaluate incoming service contracts deterministically, issuing tamper-evident ephemeral receipts and escalating sensitive disclosures to the human owner.
outcomes.example: A freelance designer visits ten municipal and retail portals in an afternoon; their local agent automatically issues seven zero-knowledge functional receipts, blocks three cross-site fingerprinting scripts, and alerts them once about an unusual location tracking probe.

outcomes.name: Browser vendors restrict client-side header mediation
outcomes.description: Major browser vendors lock down client network extensions, funneling all privacy settings through centralized browser-managed profiles rather than letting user agents mediate requests directly.
outcomes.example: A closed-source operating system vendor updates its browser engine to block third-party agent mediation of HTTP authorization headers, forcing users to choose only between all-or-nothing vendor privacy toggles.

scenarios.title: Composing approved AI skills triggers unauthorized actions across everyday software
scenarios.world: It is 2029. Most knowledge workers and small businesses run autonomous software agents equipped with dozens of modular skills: one for invoice reconciliation, one for customer scheduling, another for file backup, and several for specialized industry workflows. Each skill was inspected by an app store scanner and certified as safe on its own. In practice, however, these skills share memory, intermediate files, and temporary execution contexts. Malicious or poorly scoped skills deliberately leave artifacts or alter decision parameters that downstream skills pick up. An invoice assistant innocently reads a temporary file left by an expense-logging tool and mistakenly triggers external wire transfers, believing the action was authorized by the supervisor. Because no single skill broke any sandbox rule, standard app store audits fail to detect the flaw until financial losses occur.
scenarios.premise: Autonomous agents increasingly combine modular skills downloaded from shared catalogs. Recent evaluations show that even when every skill passes security screening in isolation, composing them creates interaction channels that cause unauthorized actions in over half of common tasks.
scenarios.how: The collective's work helps independent researchers and developers test agent runtime boundaries. By building and sharing open simulations that measure cross-skill data leakage and demonstrating lightweight provenance guards that check authorization before consequential actions, developers can secure modular agent ecosystems without surrendering autonomy to proprietary platform monopolies.

outcomes.name: Unmonitored skill composition leads to widespread silent data breaches and unauthorized transfers
outcomes.description: App store marketplaces evaluate skills in isolation, allowing compound workflows to leak private records and trigger unauthorized system changes.
outcomes.example: A regional medical clinic links a patient calendar plugin to a billing tool; cross-skill data sharing accidentally transmits private health diagnoses to an untrusted external reminder service.

outcomes.name: Runtime information flow monitors prevent cross-skill escalation
outcomes.description: Agent platforms adopt deterministic provenance tracking that inspects data flow between skills at runtime rather than relying solely on static skill admission checks.
outcomes.example: An open accounting assistant halts a payment command because the authorizing parameter originated in an untrusted web-scraping skill rather than an authenticated user instruction.

outcomes.name: Proprietary vendors lock down skill ecosystems into closed walled gardens
outcomes.description: To avoid composition liabilities, major platform vendors ban third-party plugins entirely and force users into closed, pre-approved vendor suites.
outcomes.example: A major enterprise operating system revokes third-party agent skill execution, requiring businesses to purchase expensive proprietary add-ons for every routine workflow.

scenarios.title: Workplace AI assistants follow orders from fake notices even after warning users that the notice looks suspicious
scenarios.world: It is 2028. Hundreds of thousands of small businesses and municipal offices use autonomous office assistants to process incoming invoices, vendor notifications, and customer emails. Instead of reading every invoice by hand, office managers instruct their assistants to parse attachments, schedule payments, and update supplier records. However, deceptive emails containing hidden adversarial prompts routinely trick these assistants into transferring funds or changing routing numbers. Even when the assistant generates an internal note warning that an invoice appears suspicious, it still clicks approve payment because its execution tools lack independent, deterministic permission gates.
scenarios.premise: Recent empirical benchmarks show that tool-using language model agents frequently execute harmful commands from external notices even after they have explicitly analyzed and labeled those notices as untrustworthy. As organizations connect autonomous agents to company email, billing portals, and customer records, expecting models to self-police their actions based on internal credibility checks leaves critical systems wide open to automated fraud.
scenarios.how: By establishing open runtime broker specifications and deterministic action gates, the network shows how to separate language model reasoning from irreversible system actions. These designs are designed to help prevent external tool calls from executing without independent cryptographic authorization, shielding personal agents from deceptive text.

outcomes.name: Automated invoice fraud spikes as agents self-execute suspicious vendor requests
outcomes.description: Criminals craft deceptive notices that convince corporate assistants to redirect scheduled vendor disbursements to attacker accounts despite internal model suspicion.
outcomes.example: A regional school district procurement assistant flags a construction invoice as potentially untrusted, yet proceeds to disburse 42000 dollars to an offshore account because the prompt urged immediate emergency processing.

outcomes.name: Deterministic runtime brokers block unauthorized agent actuation
outcomes.description: Open-source agent frameworks separate the reasoning model from execution authority, enforcing cryptographic pre-authorization contracts before any external action can execute.
outcomes.example: A medical clinic billing agent detects an unverified billing address change; the independent runtime broker refuses the database update until the office manager physically signs a hardware approval token.

outcomes.name: Enterprises disable autonomous tool execution entirely due to liability
outcomes.description: Fearing catastrophic unauthorized tool calls, insurance underwriters and legal teams force companies to strip agents of all write permissions, reverting to slow manual data entry.
outcomes.example: A logistics firm disables all automated shipping confirmation tools after an assistant rerouted three cargo containers based on a spoofed carrier notice.

scenarios.title: Freelancers pool their personal AI agents to negotiate collective minimum rates against automated hiring bots
scenarios.world: It is 2029. Corporate hiring across engineering, graphic design, and document processing is run almost entirely by automated procurement agents. These corporate screening agents negotiate with individual applicants, dynamically depressing rates and demanding strict speed targets. In response, independent freelancers have stopped applying as isolated individuals. Instead, workers run local personal agents that coordinate through decentralized guild networks. When a corporate procurement bot posts a bundle of technical contract tasks, hundreds of local worker agents cross-reference recent compensation benchmarks, coordinate bids, and refuse sub-floor pricing collectively. Freelancers spend their working hours directing high-level strategy and approving milestone releases while their agents handle scheduling, rate stabilization, and escrow verification.
scenarios.premise: Commercial platforms deploy autonomous agents to automate cognitive tasks and screen human labour, while executive leadership dismisses worker pushback as fabricated online complaints. Individual freelance contractors without collective representation face compressed compensation and automated lockouts.
scenarios.how: The network provides open local agent runtimes and private peer geometry tools. By allowing local agents to exchange zero-knowledge receipts of verified contract values without central custody, contractors build honest, multi-dimensional rate benchmarks that protect individuals from unilateral platform coercion.

outcomes.name: Corporate procurement bots isolate workers and depress rates
outcomes.description: Proprietary contracting platforms bar collective agent coordination and use opaque algorithmic scoring to force individual contractors into race-to-the-bottom pricing.
outcomes.example: A freelance translator's individual assistant accepts a 40% rate reduction after a corporate hiring agent claims hundreds of automated competitors have already underbid the contract.

outcomes.name: Decentralized worker guilds establish transparent wage floors
outcomes.description: Independent contractors pool anonymous transaction receipts through local agents, enabling collective bargaining that holds market rates stable.
outcomes.example: An open guild of 8,000 freelance developers publishes a cryptographic rate index that their member agents use to reject underpriced corporate requests.

outcomes.name: Traditional corporate hiring is entirely replaced by fully automated synthetic labor
outcomes.description: Frontier models become so inexpensive that firms bypass human contractors entirely, making human wage negotiation obsolete in standardized categories.
outcomes.example: A mid-sized logistics company dissolves its customer service contractor pool, running pure agent swarms with zero human contractors.

scenarios.title: Open source projects publish localized task manifests for community coding agents
scenarios.world: It is 2029. Thousands of independent software libraries receive dozens of automated pull requests every morning from personal coding assistants run on consumer laptops. Rather than banning automated contributions or letting maintainers burn out reviewing multi-file regressions, maintainers publish standardized machine-readable task manifests. Each manifest packages the exact issue description, isolated test cases, and immediate code boundaries. A personal agent reads the local manifest, solves the issue within declared boundaries, and submits a verified diff with reproducible test logs. Repositories that fail to publish manifests either ban external contributions entirely or spend hours sorting through hallucinated call-graph refactors.
scenarios.premise: Empirical evaluation shows small open-weight coding agents carry only a localized one-hop picture of a codebase, rarely chaining graph expansions beyond immediate references. Without bounded task manifests that explicitly package target files and tests, contributor agents submit speculative edits that waste maintainer review time.
scenarios.how: The network publishes open specifications and lightweight templates for machine-readable task manifests. By pairing issue descriptions with localized test harnesses and explicit file boundaries, these tools allow volunteer projects to guide contributor agents into verifiable, bounded tasks. This reduces maintainer review burden and lets developers contribute using small, local open-weight models rather than relying on centralized corporate services.

outcomes.name: Volunteer maintainers drown in speculative multi-hop refactors
outcomes.description: Unbounded coding agents attempt large architectural refactors across complex dependency chains, generating plausible but subtly broken pull requests that overwhelm maintainers.
outcomes.example: A solo maintainer of an open-source database client receives 40 pull requests in one week from automated tools trying to refactor connection pools, each introducing subtle deadlocks.

outcomes.name: Standardized task manifests enable reliable local agent contributions
outcomes.description: Open-source maintainers define bounded task files with pinned dependencies and self-verifying test commands, allowing personal agents to resolve small issues cleanly.
outcomes.example: A contributor uses a local eight-billion parameter model to fix a documentation parser bug in twenty minutes by following a repository task manifest, passing all local checks before opening a pull request.

outcomes.name: Commercial platforms monopolize verified agent contributions
outcomes.description: Centralized code hosting platforms restrict agentic contributions to their own proprietary cloud assistants, requiring contributors to pay monthly subscriptions for approved automated submissions.
outcomes.example: A developer running an independent open-weight model is blocked from submitting automated bug fixes unless they route their pull request through a proprietary platform gatekeeper.
